subject.title: [Bug P2] scheduleReconnect() has no max retry limit — infinite reconnect loop

question: Should `GatewayClient` keep unlimited reconnects by default with an opt-in cap for short-lived callers, or should OpenClaw change the default reconnect policy globally?
rationale: The unbounded scheduler is clear in source, but node-host recovery appears to rely on unlimited reconnects, so the permanent retry contract and caller opt-in surface require maintainer intent.

options.title: Opt-in bounded reconnect
options.body: Keep unlimited reconnects as the default and add a package-level `maxReconnectAttempts` policy only for maintainer-approved short-lived clients.

options.title: Global retry cap
options.body: Make every `GatewayClient` stop after a fixed number of attempts, accepting upgrade risk for long-lived node hosts during extended outages.

options.title: Document unlimited retries
options.body: Treat unlimited reconnects as intentional and close the report only if maintainers accept the resource-risk tradeoff and document the recovery model.

recommendation.title: Opt-in bounded reconnect
recommendation.body: Keep unlimited reconnects as the default and add a package-level `maxReconnectAttempts` policy only for maintainer-approved short-lived clients.

likelyOwner.reason: The gateway WebSocket control-plane history and active package-client extraction both route most directly to this owner.
